Build a person-interval panel for survival (hazard) models

build_survival_panel.Rd

Turns HRMIS snapshots into the table a model of exits is fitted on: one row per person and interval between two snapshots in which they could leave, with how long they were at risk (exposure), whether and how they left by the next snapshot (exit_type), and their covariates (and pay, if asked for) at the start of the interval.

Usage

build_survival_panel(personnel, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
build_survival_panel(
  personnel,
  contracts = NULL,
  tenure_col,
  salary_col = NULL,
  status_col = "employment_status",
  covariate_cols = NULL,
  personnel_id_col = "personnel_id",
  ref_date_col = "ref_date",
  contract_id_col = "contract_id",
  select_contract = c("highest_paid", "lowest_paid"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_dbi'
build_survival_panel(
  personnel,
  contracts = NULL,
  tenure_col,
  salary_col = NULL,
  status_col = "employment_status",
  covariate_cols = NULL,
  personnel_id_col = "personnel_id",
  ref_date_col = "ref_date",
  contract_id_col = "contract_id",
  select_contract = c("highest_paid", "lowest_paid"),
  ...
)

# Default S3 method
build_survival_panel(personnel, ...)

Arguments

personnel

Personnel snapshots: one row per person and ref_date, as a data frame or a lazy database table (tbl_dbi).

...

Not used.

contracts

Contract snapshots (one row per contract and ref_date, of the same kind as personnel), or NULL (the default) to build the panel from personnel alone. Needed for pay and for contract covariates such as occupation; give salary_col with it.

tenure_col

Character. The personnel column with years of service, e.g. from compute_tenure_panel(). It must count from hiring, not from the first snapshot.

salary_col

Character or NULL. The contracts pay column, summed across a person's contracts and carried into the panel. Deflate it first (deflate_to_real()) to compare years. To model pay, cut it into bands (e.g. quintiles) and name the band column in fit_survival_model()'s covariate_cols (see there). Required with contracts.

status_col

Character or NULL. The personnel status column, default "employment_status": "active" can leave, "pensioner" has retired. NULL, for data with no status, treats everyone on the payroll as active, so every exit is "other".

covariate_cols

Character vector or NULL. Columns to carry into the panel, from personnel (e.g. gender) or contracts (e.g. occupation, from the contract chosen by select_contract).

personnel_id_col, ref_date_col, contract_id_col

Character. The person, snapshot date and contract id columns.

select_contract

"highest_paid" (the default) or "lowest_paid": which contract the contract covariates come from when a person has several. Ties go to the lowest contract id.

Value

A survival_panel for fit_survival_model(): a data.table (a lazy table for a tbl_dbi) with one row per person and interval:

personnel_id_col, ref_date_col

The person and the start of the interval.

next_date

The next snapshot, where the interval ends.

tenure_col

Years of service at the start (NA kept).

exposure

Years at risk: the interval's length, or half of it for someone who left.

exit_type

At the next snapshot: "none" (still active), "retired" (a pensioner) or "other" (gone, or any other status).

salary_col

With contracts: total pay at the start; NA with no contract.

covariate_cols

As at the start of the interval.

It remembers the column arguments, so fit_survival_model() needs none.

Details

Model. A Poisson regression of exits with a log(exposure) offset on this panel is a piecewise-constant proportional hazards model; fit_survival_model() fits one per exit type (cause-specific hazards).

Two exit types, from fixed statuses. Only "active" and "pensioner" are read from status_col: an active person who is a pensioner at the next snapshot retired, and one who is gone or has any other status (e.g. "deceased", "transferred") left otherwise. Recode your statuses to these two first if they differ.

Risk set and censoring. Everyone active at a snapshot that has a next one; pensioners are not at risk. The last snapshot is right-censored: it adds no rows, and someone still in service then never counts as a leaver.

Left truncation. Someone in service when the panel starts enters at the tenure first seen and adds nothing to earlier tenures, which is right as long as tenure_col counts from hiring.

Exits and returns. Absence at the next snapshot is an exit, counted as half the interval at risk; someone who reappears is at risk again from there.

Intervals. An interval runs to the next snapshot in the data, so monthly or irregular snapshots work: exposure is always in years (January 2020 is 31/366), and a snapshot missing for everyone makes the interval longer rather than counting as exits.

Duplicates. A person seen twice at one snapshot is kept once, with a warning: the row first by status, then with the lowest tenure (missing values last). Rows that tie on both may differ in which one each backend keeps.

See also

fit_survival_model() to model the exits; compute_service_table() for expected years of service by tenure without covariates.

Examples

library(data.table)
#> 
#> Attaching package: ‘data.table’
#> The following object is masked from ‘package:base’:
#> 
#>     %notin%
contracts <- as.data.table(bra_hrmis_contract)
personnel <- as.data.table(bra_hrmis_personnel)
tenure <- compute_tenure_panel(contracts)
personnel <- merge(personnel, tenure, by = c("personnel_id", "ref_date"), all.x = TRUE)

# from personnel alone, with gender
panel <- build_survival_panel(
  personnel, tenure_col = "tenure_years", covariate_cols = "gender"
)
panel[, .N, by = exit_type]
#>    exit_type     N
#>       <char> <int>
#> 1:     other   330
#> 2:      none  9173
#> 3:   retired   250

# with real pay and the occupation of each person's highest-paid contract
